outcome_definition: DESIGN (paper's definition): 'the ratio of the SNP sites that can be used to design primers to the total number of SNP sites'. Here 100/100.
note: the paper's 'assay design success rate of 100%'

outcome_definition: WORK (paper's definition): 'the number of SNP sites that can generate genotype calls via primers to the number of SNP sites with successfully designed primers'. The paper's 92% is 92/100 = (71 polymorphic + 21 monomorphic-or-heterozygous)/100; that is the fraction that produced ANY call, not the fraction that produced a TWO-ALLELE (usable) call, which is 71%. This extract records both so neither can be quoted as the other.
note: derived: 100 - 8 (the only category that did not amplify)

outcome_definition: AMPLIFICATION: 100 - 8 = 92 of 100 assays 'generated a useful amplification signal'. Identical to the paper's 92% work rate by its own arithmetic (71 + 21), which is why the paper and this extract must be read carefully: amplifying is not the same as being a usable marker.
note: derived: identical to the paper's work rate by its own arithmetic

outcome_definition: USABLE (paper's category): '71 (71%) of these MKAMs were found to be polymorphic'. This is the only count in the paper that means 'a working, informative assay on this material'.
note: the paper's own count; this is the number a breeder would call 'working'

outcome_definition: UNUSABLE (paper's category): '21 (21%) were monomorphic and/or heterozygous type and were deemed unusable as markers'. Amplified but not informative on LM11 x CML25.
NO SIGNAL (paper's category): 'The remaining 8 (8%) failed to generate a useful amplification signal and thus were unusable'.

SUPPLEMENT COVERAGE, not an outcome: supporting data S2 prints a primer triple for 92 of the 100 sites. This is what the file shows, NOT a design rate -- the paper claims 100% design success and the missing 8 are not identified anywhere.
